_comment: Registered settings for feature_search.py. Changing a value here is a
specification change and is recorded in data/feature_search_metrics.json
under config_hash. Targets, learners and gates are data, not code, so a
new target or a tighter gate is a config edit with no new code path.

restrict.label: has_enacted_restrictive
restrict.description: county has ever enacted a restrictive instrument (moratorium, zoning restriction, ban)

restrict_profile.label: has_enacted_restrictive
restrict_profile.description: same outcome, county profile variables only (no outcome-derived information of any kind); the weights a client-facing score may use

moratorium.label: has_enacted_moratorium
moratorium.description: county has ever enacted a moratorium specifically

conversion.label: has_enacted_restrictive
conversion.description: among counties with recorded local opposition before any enactment, which went on to enact a restriction

stability_selection._comment: Only penalties sparse enough to keep the expected number of falsely selected variables at or below max_expected_false at the threshold are used (Meinshausen-Buhlmann bound). The bound decides the penalty range, so selection probability carries error control rather than being a tuning artifact.

ebm._comment: Spec 008 US4. Explainable Boosting Machine (interpret-core) on one target, scored on that target's registered CV folds, then refit once on the whole frame for per-variable shape tables (data/feature_search_shapes.json). Main effects only, so every shape is one readable curve. max_bins 32 (default 1024) keeps each curve chartable: 5-fold AUC on restrict_profile was 0.798 at 32 bins vs 0.799 at 1024, while 1024 bins carry bin-to-bin noise. A challenger: choose_promotions() never reads it. Runs only where feature_search.py runs (feature-search.yml, weekly).

weight_filter._comment: Local-level Kalman filter on each feature's held-out importance. process_sd is how far a true importance may move between runs; a larger value adapts faster and smooths less.
